m-tallahassee|2026-07-14|2ae39896|dc87de.title: History/Facts & Issues The Downtown Redevelopment District has experienced substantial investment in recent years. However, much of this investment has been concentrated in office and residential development. Sub-Area #1 – North Monroe and Sub-Area #2 – Downtown Core continue to lack the concentration of retail, hospitality, entertainment, and cultural uses necessary to support the broader vision of a vibrant 18-hour downtown. The Downtown Improvement Authority has identified the high cost of converting existing commercial space into retail and hospitality uses as one of the primary barriers to investment. While the existing Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP) provides valuable assistance, its dollar-for-dollar matching requirement and maximum grant amount of $200,000 have limited its effectiveness for projects involving significant tenant improvements and adaptive reuse that would be needed for more active uses.
